This forgets d -= 9.
Correct!

What is the value of c after the following code is executed?

int c = 0;
for (int i = 1; i <= 50; i++) {
    int n = i;
    int s = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        s += n % 10;
        n /= 10;
    }
    if (s % 5 == 0) {
        c++;
    }
}

generalfeedback.text: Why: c counts the numbers 1..50 whose digit sum is a multiple of 5: 5, 14, 19, 23, 28, 32, 37, 41, 46, 50. c = 10. Trap: 10 = 50 / 5 looks like counting multiples of 5, but the numbers counted are different.

feedback.text: This uses i < 50.
This tests s == 5 (forgets sum 10).
Digit sums 10 count too (19, 28, 37, 46).
Between 1 and 50 only digit sums 5 and 10 occur (no number here has digit sum 15).
Correct!

generalfeedback.text: Why: For negative n, / 2 truncates toward 0 and % 7 is negative. n after each pass: -25 -12 -6 -3 -1 0. The first n with n % 7 == 0 is 0, reached after 6 passes. Trap: -50 % 7 = -1, not 6, and -25 / 2 = -12.

c counts halvings, not the 7.
This rounds -25 / 2 down to -13; C++ truncates toward 0 and gives -12.
Correct!
